name: Shropshire

licensing.selective: No selective licensing scheme (the council's 2026 civil penalty policy notes there are no selective licensing areas).
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme: HMOs with five or more people from two or more households need a mandatory licence, whatever the number of storeys.
licensing.fee: £1,200 for an HMO licence for up to five bedrooms plus £170 for each extra bedroom, valid five years (2024/25 application form)

housing: Shropshire is a large rural county with Shrewsbury as its main town and a ring of market towns: Oswestry, Ludlow, Bridgnorth, Market Drayton and Whitchurch. Older homes include timber-framed and Georgian town houses, stone and brick cottages, and farm conversions, many of them listed or in conservation areas. Much of the countryside is off the gas grid. Private renting is a little below the national average, and HMOs are found mainly in Shrewsbury.
checkinTips: Rural homes off the gas grid: photograph the oil tank, its gauge level and the boiler, or the LPG tank and meter, and note any wood burner and its sweep record.
Cottages and farm conversions with private drainage: record the septic tank or treatment plant cover and any service record left for the tenant.
Timber-framed and listed houses in Shrewsbury, Ludlow and Much Wenlock: photograph beams, uneven floors, old windows and any damp or cracks in plaster.
Homes near the Severn in Shrewsbury and Bridgnorth: check ground floors, skirting boards and gardens for signs of past flooding.
New-build estates around Shrewsbury and Shifnal: photograph snagging items, sealant, paintwork and the garden, and note who maintains shared areas.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact Shropshire Council's private sector housing team, which can inspect homes and take action against landlords.
